villain.rocket.event1.body: A Rocket grunt buys a Slowpoke tail at the route stop. The child selling it counts the money twice; the grunt watches the road instead of the child. When he sees your badge, he says, “Stay in your lane, junior.”

intro: A Rocket grunt buys a Slowpoke tail at the route stop. The child selling it counts the money twice; the grunt watches the road instead of the child. When he sees your badge, he says, “Stay in your lane, junior.”
outro: The truck carries an ordinary delivery permit. That bothers you more than the uniform. You remember the plate and the company printed below it. If this is a business, somewhere it keeps records.

villain.rocket.ending.title: Some Things Stop
villain.rocket.ending.body: Rocket’s logo comes off the trucks. The ledger gives the missing names somewhere to go: into statements, searches, and questions that can no longer be dismissed as rumor.

climax: Rocket’s logo comes off the trucks. The ledger gives the missing names somewhere to go: into statements, searches, and questions that can no longer be dismissed as rumor.
outro: The Marowak remains on the hill. You sit nearby without asking it to call this justice. Before leaving, you check the route stop for new notices. A victory can end a battle; keeping its promise takes longer.

villain.magma.event1.body: A Magma speaker stands on a stump above a dry stream. “The land remembers,” he tells the crowd. One listener holds an empty water can. Another holds a photograph of a flooded home.

intro: A Magma speaker stands on a stump above a dry stream. “The land remembers,” he tells the crowd. One listener holds an empty water can. Another holds a photograph of a flooded home.
outro: Their losses are real. His answer is to make everyone else lose something too. You note the marked survey stakes beside the stream. The next claim you hear about saving the land will have to answer for those stakes.

villain.magma.ending.title: Water in the Well
villain.magma.ending.body: The wells refill slowly. The device is stopped, but a stopped machine cannot put a season’s rain back into the fields. Neighbors take turns carrying water to the highest houses.

climax: The wells refill slowly. The device is stopped, but a stopped machine cannot put a season’s rain back into the fields. Neighbors take turns carrying water to the highest houses.
outro: The stuffed Vulpix has new hands holding it. You hear the old sermon at a different roadside stall, then hear someone ask where the water went. This time the question is louder than the sermon.

villain.aqua.event1.body: An Aqua grunt gives swimming lessons beside the river. The children trust him because he gets into the cold water first. Then he tells them the river is a god, and gods take what they want.

intro: An Aqua grunt gives swimming lessons beside the river. The children trust him because he gets into the cold water first. Then he tells them the river is a god, and gods take what they want.
outro: You ask who decides what the river wants. He smiles and calls the children in for another lesson. Downstream, painted stakes mark a waterline well above the houses. You remember their height.

villain.aqua.ending.title: A Shore Worth Keeping
villain.aqua.ending.body: The harbor survives behind sandbags and repaired walls. Some shorelines are gone. The tide chart can no longer pass for a prophecy: it was a schedule, and people know who wrote it.

climax: The harbor survives behind sandbags and repaired walls. Some shorelines are gone. The tide chart can no longer pass for a prophecy: it was a schedule, and people know who wrote it.
outro: The shell on your belt is still warm. You hold it toward the sea and hear only water. On the quay, a child practices a swimming stroke with a parent close enough to help.

villain.galactic.event1.body: A Galactic volunteer offers a tourist tea and a careful explanation. Emotion, he says, is a wound. Cyrus intends to close it. The tourist tips him for being kind.

intro: A Galactic volunteer offers a tourist tea and a careful explanation. Emotion, he says, is a wound. Cyrus intends to close it. The tourist tips him for being kind.
outro: You ask whether anyone gets to refuse the cure. His answer begins with numbers and never reaches the tourist. You keep the leaflet. There is a difference between easing pain and removing the person who feels it.

villain.galactic.ending.title: An Imperfect Sky
villain.galactic.ending.body: Cyrus enters the Distortion gate willingly. When it closes, the stars hold still. The shrine keeper asks you the time; later, he remembers that he already asked.

climax: Cyrus enters the Distortion gate willingly. When it closes, the stars hold still. The shrine keeper asks you the time; later, he remembers that he already asked.
outro: An ordinary argument starts in the square about whose turn it is to repair a fence. Nobody agrees. Nobody vanishes. Your partner leans against your leg, and for a moment an imperfect world feels like something worth defending.

villain.plasma.event1.body: A Plasma sage speaks gently to a child holding a battered Poké Ball. “If you love it,” he says, “put it down.” The child obeys, then walks away crying. The Pokémon waits beside the ball.

intro: A Plasma sage speaks gently to a child holding a battered Poké Ball. “If you love it,” he says, “put it down.” The child obeys, then walks away crying. The Pokémon waits beside the ball.
outro: You wait too, until the child looks back. Neither of them seems liberated. You want to know what this movement offers the partners it separates, and who is allowed to ask them what they want.

villain.plasma.ending.title: The Choice to Stay
villain.plasma.ending.body: N leaves the region before the speeches begin. Plasma dissolves, but the flyers remain. A slogan is easy to print after the people who used it have changed their names.

climax: N leaves the region before the speeches begin. Plasma dissolves, but the flyers remain. A slogan is easy to print after the people who used it have changed their names.
outro: You think of the wounded Patrat and the question N could not stop asking. At the next rest stop, your partner settles beside you without being called. You make room. That is an answer you can keep giving.

villain.flare.event1.body: A Flare recruiter studies your starter, then places a sticker on your jacket. “You passed.” He has not asked either of you a question. Behind him, another trainer is turned away without an explanation.

intro: A Flare recruiter studies your starter, then places a sticker on your jacket. “You passed.” He has not asked either of you a question. Behind him, another trainer is turned away without an explanation.
outro: The sticker is a small thing to carry. The list it belongs to is not. You watch where the rejected trainer goes and remember the recruiter’s word: worthy.

villain.flare.ending.title: Names, Not Categories
villain.flare.ending.body: The Weapon is dismantled in guarded pieces. The printed lists are harder to recover. People whose names appeared on them begin asking who decided, who agreed, and who looked away.

climax: The Weapon is dismantled in guarded pieces. The printed lists are harder to recover. People whose names appeared on them begin asking who decided, who agreed, and who looked away.
outro: The mark on your jacket cannot tell anyone what you are. You look at the partners beside you, each different from the others, each here for reasons no list could have measured.

villain.skull.event1.body: Two Skull grunts demand your shoes. Their pose is practiced; the demand is not. One keeps glancing at the other for the next line. They are younger than they want you to notice.

intro: Two Skull grunts demand your shoes. Their pose is practiced; the demand is not. One keeps glancing at the other for the next line. They are younger than they want you to notice.
outro: You look past the bandanas. Someone taught them that taking a thing would prove they belonged. You want to meet the person who made belonging cost this much.

villain.skull.ending.title: A Place After the House
villain.skull.ending.body: The Skull house gets a new tenant. Its former residents need addresses, meals, and something to do when nobody is watching. Some find those things quickly. Others keep their bags packed.

climax: The Skull house gets a new tenant. Its former residents need addresses, meals, and something to do when nobody is watching. Some find those things quickly. Others keep their bags packed.
outro: Guzma still has the unsent letter. Plumeria still knows which children have not checked in. You remember their names when you pass through town. A team should be able to ask for help without first winning a fight.

villain.yell.event1.body: Team Yell crowds the entrance of a small-town gym. They shout the name of the girl they say they support so loudly that she cannot answer a question from the door. Tickets for her show go on sale in three weeks.

intro: Team Yell crowds the entrance of a small-town gym. They shout the name of the girl they say they support so loudly that she cannot answer a question from the door. Tickets for her show go on sale in three weeks.
outro: You wait until the shouting pauses and ask whether she wants company. The organizers answer for her. That is the part you remember as you continue down the road.

villain.yell.ending.title: Her Own Voice
villain.yell.ending.body: Marnie’s tour is cancelled. The sponsor calls it a change of direction. The leaked messages give her a more accurate name for what happened, even when the accounts reposting them disappear.

climax: Marnie’s tour is cancelled. The sponsor calls it a change of direction. The leaked messages give her a more accurate name for what happened, even when the accounts reposting them disappear.
outro: At home, she sings without an introduction. There is no campaign slogan attached to the song. The people listening wait for her to finish before they answer.

villain.macroCosmos.event1.body: A sponsorship truck arrives while workers paint over the gym’s local sigil. The mayor signs the agreement for a camera. A young trainer asks whether the old sign can stay; nobody holding a microphone hears her.

intro: A sponsorship truck arrives while workers paint over the gym’s local sigil. The mayor signs the agreement for a camera. A young trainer asks whether the old sign can stay; nobody holding a microphone hears her.
outro: The contract promises a future for the town. You want to know who gets to choose that future once the paint dries. On the truck, a drone turns to keep your badge in frame.

villain.macroCosmos.ending.title: Who Owns the Story
villain.macroCosmos.ending.body: Macro Cosmos restructures under a new name. The succession document remains in circulation. Beside your name is the phrase that still refuses to explain itself: The First.

climax: Macro Cosmos restructures under a new name. The succession document remains in circulation. Beside your name is the phrase that still refuses to explain itself: The First.
outro: The drone is still somewhere overhead. You make the next decision with your team gathered close enough to hear you. A camera can record the choice. It cannot make it for you.

villain.star.event1.body: A Star captain sits on the school steps, watching the gate. He is not waiting for a challenger. Every time younger students arrive, he stands until they are safely inside.

intro: A Star captain sits on the school steps, watching the gate. He is not waiting for a challenger. Every time younger students arrive, he stands until they are safely inside.
outro: He calls it keeping watch. The school calls it causing trouble. You ask what happened the last time nobody watched the gate. His silence gives you a reason to stay interested.

villain.star.ending.title: The Gate Opens
villain.star.ending.body: The school issues its statement. The adults responsible still have questions to answer. The younger students have places to go now, and people who notice when they do not arrive.

climax: The school issues its statement. The adults responsible still have questions to answer. The younger students have places to go now, and people who notice when they do not arrive.
outro: You keep your copy of the small list. It has become more than evidence: names to check on, promises to follow up. At the gate, someone who used to wait outside walks in beside a friend.

extra.cubone.event1.body: A child rehearses a school play beside the road, wearing a skull mask that slips over their eyes. You steady it before it falls. The bone is real, and carefully polished.

intro: A child rehearses a school play beside the road, wearing a skull mask that slips over their eyes. You steady it before it falls. The bone is real, and carefully polished.
outro: The child knows every line of the play except who made the mask. You remember how gently they hold it when they take it off. Someone’s grief has reached this road before you.

extra.cubone.ending.title: What the Stones Hold
extra.cubone.ending.body: Twenty-seven cairns stand on the hill. The empty place beside them still troubles you. It no longer gets to decide whom you will lose next.

climax: Twenty-seven cairns stand on the hill. The empty place beside them still troubles you. It no longer gets to decide whom you will lose next.
outro: You set one loose stone back where the rain moved it. Your partner waits while you finish. Remembering the dead does not have to mean rehearsing your own absence.

extra.yamask.event1.body: A mask in a shop window stops you mid-step. The shopkeeper calls it a costume. When you ask whose face it was modeled on, he busies himself with a shelf that is already straight.

intro: A mask in a shop window stops you mid-step. The shopkeeper calls it a costume. When you ask whose face it was modeled on, he busies himself with a shelf that is already straight.
outro: You look again before leaving. The expression seems familiar, but familiarity is not a name. You decide to remember the face without inventing an owner for it.

extra.yamask.ending.title: A Face She Keeps
extra.yamask.ending.body: The widow has stopped gambling. She does not offer you an explanation, and you do not demand one. Her smile belongs to the person sitting across the table from you, whatever the mirrors might say.

climax: The widow has stopped gambling. She does not offer you an explanation, and you do not demand one. Her smile belongs to the person sitting across the table from you, whatever the mirrors might say.
outro: Outside, you catch your reflection in a dark window. You touch your own cheek and keep walking. Some questions deserve care before they deserve an answer.

extra.hypno.event1.body: A missing-person poster at the route stop shows a girl in a yellow shirt. Three years of sunlight have faded the color. Someone has kept the contact details legible in fresh ink.

intro: A missing-person poster at the route stop shows a girl in a yellow shirt. Three years of sunlight have faded the color. Someone has kept the contact details legible in fresh ink.
outro: You read the date and the name. Then you read them again. The poster is evidence of an absence; the new ink is evidence that somebody is still looking.

extra.hypno.ending.title: A Name Remembered
extra.hypno.ending.body: The route board has fresh notices. Some old ones are marked FOUND. The children who returned do not owe strangers the story of what happened to them.

climax: The route board has fresh notices. Some old ones are marked FOUND. The children who returned do not owe strangers the story of what happened to them.
outro: A parent traces the letters of a name on the board before taking the paper down. You leave them the space to do it. Later, when the road seems too quiet, you say your partner’s name and wait for the answer.

extra.phantump.event1.body: A small shoe lies beside the path. No matching shoe, no fresh footprints, and no grass growing through the laces. You stop your partner before either of you steps over it.

intro: A small shoe lies beside the path. No matching shoe, no fresh footprints, and no grass growing through the laces. You stop your partner before either of you steps over it.
outro: You mark the place in your memory: the split tree, the pale stone, the bend in the path. If someone comes looking, “somewhere in the woods” will not be enough.

extra.phantump.ending.title: The List Stops Growing
extra.phantump.ending.body: The teacher stops singing. No new names appear in the notebook. The shoe is gone, though you cannot tell who took it or whether they needed it.

climax: The teacher stops singing. No new names appear in the notebook. The shoe is gone, though you cannot tell who took it or whether they needed it.
outro: You remember the painted stones by their drawings, not their number. On the way out of the woods, you check that your partner is beside you. You both wait until the path is clear.

extra.mimikyu.event1.body: A child has taped a drawing of Pikachu low on a roadside tree. The tail bends the wrong way. All four corners are fixed carefully against the rain.

intro: A child has taped a drawing of Pikachu low on a roadside tree. The tail bends the wrong way. All four corners are fixed carefully against the rain.
outro: Someone wanted a Pokémon to know it was loved. You wonder whether a creature passing this tree would recognize the name under the picture, or only the care that held it there.

extra.mimikyu.ending.title: Room in the Light
extra.mimikyu.ending.body: The thrift shop places the worn costume at the front of the window. The price tag is still there. So is a small repaired seam that was not there before.

climax: The thrift shop places the worn costume at the front of the window. The price tag is still there. So is a small repaired seam that was not there before.
outro: You do not lift the cloth. You stand where whoever is inside can see you, then give it room to choose. Being noticed should not have to mean being exposed.

extra.drifloon.event1.body: A purple balloon drifts above the trees. A child holds its string on the adjoining path, where the wind is stronger. For a moment the child’s feet seem lighter than they should.

intro: A purple balloon drifts above the trees. A child holds its string on the adjoining path, where the wind is stronger. For a moment the child’s feet seem lighter than they should.
outro: You call across and keep the child in sight until the path descends. The balloon pulls once against its string. It feels less like a toy when it knows you are watching.

extra.drifloon.ending.title: Stay Within Reach
extra.drifloon.ending.body: On the later road, another child holds a purple balloon on a short string. You stop close enough to speak. The child points to a companion just ahead, then calls them back.

climax: On the later road, another child holds a purple balloon on a short string. You stop close enough to speak. The child points to a companion just ahead, then calls them back.
outro: You wait until they are together before continuing. The wind follows the road. For once, the small hand holding the string is not the only hand within reach.

extra.parasect.event1.body: A Paras emerges from the grass with a mushroom too bright for the shade. Its body pauses, but the cap turns a fraction farther toward you. Then both move on together.

intro: A Paras emerges from the grass with a mushroom too bright for the shade. Its body pauses, but the cap turns a fraction farther toward you. Then both move on together.
outro: You watch the place where they disappeared. The question is not whether something is alive. It is who is choosing where it goes.

extra.parasect.ending.title: Who Answers
extra.parasect.ending.body: The trainer’s replacement calls her absence a sabbatical. Her empty chair still hums faintly. You ask when anyone last heard from her, and wait through the first easy answer.

climax: The trainer’s replacement calls her absence a sabbatical. Her empty chair still hums faintly. You ask when anyone last heard from her, and wait through the first easy answer.
outro: You leave her name where it can be found again. At camp, your partner refuses a game and curls up instead. You let it. A small refusal can be a reassuring sound.

extra.mewtwo.event1.body: A torn laboratory patch lies half-buried beside the route. Its logo resembles the one on a Department Store advertisement. Under the dirt, the stitching reads PROJECT — 0001.

intro: A torn laboratory patch lies half-buried beside the route. Its logo resembles the one on a Department Store advertisement. Under the dirt, the stitching reads PROJECT — 0001.
outro: You memorize the number before putting the patch away. A project has a purpose, a maker, and someone who decided it could begin. You intend to learn which of those the number is hiding.

extra.mewtwo.ending.title: More Than a Number
extra.mewtwo.ending.body: The laboratory seal is dated this morning. Through the glass, the clipboard reads 0001, 0002, 0003. Beside the third number is your name, spelled correctly.

climax: The laboratory seal is dated this morning. Through the glass, the clipboard reads 0001, 0002, 0003. Beside the third number is your name, spelled correctly.
outro: You copy the date and the name instead of accepting the label. Your partner waits at your side while you finish. Whatever the laboratory expected you to become, it will have to account for the choices you have already made.
